summary: Spiced lamb meatballs roasted in one tray on a bed of peppers and onions. A forgiving first oven dish: nothing is browned in a pan first, the meatballs are rolled by hand, and minced lamb is cooked right through rather than to a judged degree of doneness.

ingredients.note: Tree nut. Omit only if you accept that the record then departs from its source.
Wheat. Binds the mixture with the egg.

ingredients.item: Red onions, each peeled and cut into 8 wedges

ingredients.quantity: The source seasons the meatball mixture and the vegetables to taste and gives no weight.

method.instruction: Heat the oven to 220°C conventional, or 200°C fan (gas mark 7). Both figures are stated by the source; neither is a conversion made here.
Put the mince, cumin, coriander, chilli flakes, parsley, mint, garlic, pistachios, lemon juice, flour, egg, salt and pepper in a large bowl and mix.
Spread the peppers and onion wedges over a large roasting pan in a single layer, turn them through the olive oil and season.
Roll the mixture into balls a little smaller than a golf ball — the source gets 20 from this quantity — and space them among the vegetables.
Take the pan out, lift the meatballs off, stir the vegetables, then set the meatballs back the other way up.

Roast for a further 15 to 20 minutes, until the meatballs are cooked all the way through. Minced lamb is safe at an internal 71°C measured in the centre of the largest ball (Health Canada, Safe cooking temperatures); the elapsed time is not the test.

yield_note: Serves 4, as stated by the source, and makes about 20 meatballs. Source times: 15 minutes preparation and 30 minutes cooking. The source gives no resting time, and none is invented here.

provenance_note: Recipe facts paraphrased from Eb Gargano's page at Easy Peasy Foodie, accessed 2026-09-14; the safety threshold is Health Canada's. Two things are recorded as the source leaves them: its stated cook time of 30 minutes is shorter than its own steps, which run 15 minutes plus a further 15 to 20; and it writes tablespoons and teaspoons without stating a millilitre value, so no spoon size is asserted here. Spoon volumes differ by country: a tablespoon defined as 15 mL holds a quarter less than one defined as 20 mL, so measure with a single spoon set rather than mixing them.

caveats: Minced lamb carries surface bacteria through the whole mixture, so it must be cooked right through — unlike a whole cut. Health Canada gives 71°C internal for ground lamb; the UK Food Standards Agency puts the general rule as 70°C held for 2 minutes and states that any meat minced or skewered all the way through should be cooked thoroughly.
Raw mince and the egg both contaminate what they touch. Wash hands, bowl and board after mixing, and do not return cooked meatballs to the unwashed plate or pan surface that held them raw.
Allergens in this record: egg, wheat flour, and pistachio (tree nut).
